newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian guards got wrong volcano in report.
newsitem.headline: Russian guards got wrong volcano in report.

text.p: Russian border guards probably made a mistake when they said a volcano in the Russian Far East had erupted for the first time in more than 70 years, Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday.
Tass said a weekend report from the border guard service about an eruption of the supposedly dormant Kranotsky peak on the remote Kamchatka peninsula had not been confirmed.
Experts believed another volcano, Karymsky, had simply become more active.

Stanislav Balesta, head of the Kamchatka centre monitoring volcanic and seismic activity, told Tass Karymsky was spewing out molten lava and sending a column of smoke five km (three miles) into the air.
There were no reports of injuries or damage.
Karymsky started erupting in January this year, blasting hot ash about seven km (four miles) into the air.
